dharana.numbering_edition: Jaideva Singh 1979 (dhāraṇā 1 = verse 24; dhāraṇā 82 = verses 105–106 and dhāraṇā 89 = verses 113–114, otherwise one verse each; dhāraṇā 112 = verse 137)
dharana.sanskrit_iast: līnaṃ mūrdhni viyat sarvam bhairavatvena bhāvayet | tat sarvam bhairavākāratejastattvaṃ samāviśet ||
dharana.sanskrit_source: GRETIL e-text, compared with Wallis's concordance, Pradīpaka and the Singh scan
dharana.rendering: Let one contemplate all of space, as Bhairava himself, dissolved in one's head; then one enters all of it as the luminous reality of Bhairava's form.
dharana.rendering_attribution: School paraphrase drawing on Jaideva Singh (1979), Christopher Wallis and Bettina Bäumer (as printed in Wallis's concordance); not a quotation.
dharana.commentary_note: Singh: by creative contemplation (bhāvanā) one imagines the vast sky as Bhairava's expression, dissolved in the space inside the head; that inner space becomes a symbol of Bhairava's infinity and the whole universe is felt bathed in his light. Wallis: 'the sky is in your head', so that the head is continuous with the sky.
dharana.technique_name: The Whole Sky Dissolved in the Head
dharana.instruction: Picture the whole sky gathered into the space inside your head, until they are one.

seat.label: Any steady, comfortable position (school addition)
seat.summary: Any steady, comfortable position: sitting on a chair, sitting on the floor with support under the hips, or lying on the back. Standing or walking slowly is also acceptable when that is easier. Choose the position in which the body needs the least effort.
seat.honesty: School addition. Verse 85 does not specify a body position. The seat is a convenience so the dharana can be practised; it is not part of the technique and makes no claim of tradition.

geometry.summary: Not a body shape. The map is the whole sky drawn into the space inside the head until the two are one continuous space.
geometry.svg_hint: a head outline whose inside opens into a wide sky
geometry.honesty: Geometry records the dharana's own map of attention, not a body shape. Locations marked 'commentarial' come from commentary, not from the verse.

reaction.name: Sky in the head
reaction.summary: School metaphor only: the small space of the head and the vast sky are felt as one luminous space. Not a biochemical or medical claim.

breath.lands_in: wherever the breath naturally ends; this door places nothing on the breath
breath.cue: Natural breath. Count about four in and four out only if it helps you settle, then let the count go. No forced hold.
breath.honesty: The counts are an optional school pacing aid, not part of the verse. Hold is always 0: this school never adds a deliberate breath-hold.

orientation.cue: Let the space inside the head and the whole sky become one
orientation.gravity: Let the floor or chair carry the body completely; there is no posture to hold
orientation.degrees_hint: No angle target: the VBT gives no posture for this dharana

attention.primary: The whole sky felt as dissolved in the space inside the head

adiyogi.verse_paraphrase: Let one contemplate all of space, as Bhairava himself, dissolved in one's head; then one enters all of it as the luminous reality of Bhairava's form.
adiyogi.method_summary: Picture the whole sky. Let it gather into the space inside your head, until the inside of the head and the sky feel like one continuous, luminous space. Rest there.

honesty.disclosure: Door 062 follows Vijñāna Bhairava Tantra dharana 62 (verse 85) in Jaideva Singh's numbering. The door-to-dharana index is a School of 112 Doorways teaching device. Singh's sequence is one edition's count, not an ancient one-to-one canon. The seat, counts, reaction and beat scripts are school additions.
honesty.notes: pairing_type is school_device: the dharana is the content, while the door index, seat and pacing are the school's.
flags: Door index = Jaideva Singh dharana number: Door 062 is dharana 62, verse 85. Other editions number differently (see dharana.numbering_variants).
The seat, breath counts, reaction metaphor, attention-map drawing and beat scripts are school devices, not part of the verse.
The English is a school paraphrase, not a quotation from any translator.
No medical claims. Reaction names are metaphors, not biochemistry.

safety.pain_rule: Pain is information. Pause, regress, or exit. Never push through sharp pain.
safety.open_seat_alternate: This door needs no particular posture: sit on a chair, sit on the floor with support, or lie down. Eyes may stay open.
safety.contraindication_notes: General practice caution only; not medical advice. Keep it light and spacious; if pressure in the head appears, let the image go and feel the feet. If anything feels distressing (dizziness, agitation, strong emotion), stop, open the eyes and rest attention on the feet and the floor.
